artists.biography: Doctor Who is a British science-fiction television programme broadcast by the BBC since 1963. The programme depicts the adventures of a Time Lord called the Doctor, exploring the universe in a time-travelling space ship called the TARDIS. The TARDIS exterior appears as a blue British police box, which was a common sight in Britain in 1963 when the series first aired. There have been many composers throughout the show's run. Notable composers are: Murray Gold (2005-2017), Segun Akinola (2017-2022), Dudley Simpson (various stories from 1964- 1980), and Peter Howell (1980-1985), among others. NOTE: Spotify and other streaming services have "Doctor Who" listed as the artist on many of Big Finish Productions' Doctor Who audio drama releases. Read more on Last.fm. Doctor Who And The Pescatons / Doctor Who Sound Effects No.19" is a 1978 release by Doctor Who, originally issued by BBC Records and later reissued by Demon Records. The album combines two distinct elements: the audio drama "Doctor Who and the Pescatons," narrated by Tom Baker, and a collection of sound effects from the BBC Radiophonic Workshop, curated as "BBC Sound Effects No.19." Musically, the album is rooted in electronic experimentation, featuring synthesizer-driven compositions and atmospheric soundscapes typical of the Radiophonic Workshop's pioneering work. The "Pescatons" segment blends spoken word with eerie electronic music, creating an immersive experience that aligns with the show's sci-fi aesthetic.

Within the Doctor Who discography, this album stands out as a unique hybrid of narrative and sound design, bridging the gap between children's entertainment and avant-garde electronic music. It reflects the creative output of the BBC Radiophonic Workshop during a period of innovation in television sound, and its inclusion of both a story and a sound effects library makes it a distinctive entry in the series' catalog. While not a commercial chart success, the album has been recognized for its historical significance and influence on electronic music and sound design, particularly within the context of British television and children's programming.
